messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 5xx & timeout surge on /v1/generate across us-west-1. p95 ~ 1.2s -> 2.7s, p99 ~ 4.1s. Error rate 5xx up 8% in last 5m. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Devon: I'm paged, looking now. any deploys in last 30m?
Maya: yes, runtime commit r1249 rolled at 4101232000. Canary looked ok but cutover finished 10m ago.
Devon: ok pulling logs + traces. grabbing traces for a sample 504s.
Jordi: from proxy traces, requests are stalling at backend connection attempt, a lot of upstream 504/gateway-timeout.
Devon: tailing inference worker logs — seeing repeated kv-cache lock waits and grpc timeouts.
Devon: log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:34:12.123Z [WARN] request_id=abc123 stall waiting kvcache.lock for 2150ms
2026-03-14T02:34:12.125Z [ERROR] request_id=abc123 backend grpc deadline exceeded
2026-03-14T02:34:12.126Z [ERROR] request_id=abc123 502 gateway from runtime
```
Sam: that lines up with r1249 change that touched KV lock acquisition ordering.
Lina: I'm taking oncall. Devon handoff to me?
Devon: SG, Lina — summary: post-deploy runtime r1249 introduced a change to k/v cache prefetch ordering -> potential lock convoy on hot prefixes. Causes p99 stalls and 5xx. Canary passed due to low traffic there. Global cutover hit hot traffic.
Lina: thanks. Immediate mitigation options? rollback, routing to fallback model, increase concurrency, or bump timeouts.
Maya: quickest is rollback to r1248. Can trigger hot rollback via deploy-bot. Also we can flip routing to older model variant but that requires traffic policy change.
Claire: support: do we have a list of customers on Dedicated us-west-1 who might see errors? I need to notify any active enterprise accounts.
Jordi: pulling slice by account — looks like 8 enterprise tenants sent requests during spike, plus general hosted traffic.
Devon: I'm hitting health endpoints on workers. Some respond slow, some 200. Not uniform.
deploy-bot: Received rollback request for runtime-service -> initiating rollback to r1248. ETA 90s for rollout start.
pagerduty: Paging: Devon acknowledged. Lina acknowledged.
Lina: rolling back now. also enabling fallback routing for heavy endpoints (/v1/generate -> variant: gen-stable-202602).
Maya: command to rollback:
```bash
# rollback single deployment
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime-service --to-revision=1248
```
Devon: running that now.
Devon: rollback started. watching deploy events.
deploy-bot: Rollback started: runtime-service -> from r1249 -> r1248. Progress: 2/6 pods updated.
Jordi: simultaneously opening temporary circuit-breaker for paths hitting long-tail tokens to reduce retries. config snippet:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
circuit_breaker:
  max_inflight: 250
  retry_policy: none
```
Sam: also recommend flushing kvcache locks on problematic instances to clear convoys: `sudo systemctl restart runtime-worker` (only on affected pods).
Lina: avoid mass restart; let rollout replace pods. only restart if specific pod stays stuck after 3 minutes.
Devon: rollback finished. deploy-bot shows all pods at r1248.
deploy-bot: Rollback completed: runtime-service now at r1248.
Maya: metrics update — p99 dropped from 4.1s -> 0.9s within 2 minutes. 5xx rate back to baseline. :thumbsup:
Claire: OK I'm sending customer notifications to impacted tenants: short incident note + mitigation and ETA for RCA.
Claire: draft: "We observed elevated error rates and timeouts in us-west-1 after a recent runtime update. We rolled back the change and service performance has returned to baseline. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a detailed RCA."
Lina: good. Also note we're scheduling a hotfix that reintroduces the r1249 change with a different lock strategy and rollout gating by prefix heat.
Devon: collecting traces + flame graphs for RCA. saving logs to /incidents/4101234567/artifacts.tar.gz
Maya: creating postmortem stub. tagging eng-runtime, eng-sre, and product.
Devon: any lingering errors? I'm seeing isolated 502s but rates are normal.
Sam: keep monitoring for 30m. if rates remain stable, close page.
Lina: handing off to follow-up oncall: Maya will own RCA and follow-up. I'll remain reachable for 30m.
Maya: taking follow-up. thanks everyone. I'll post RCA timeline in #postmortems in a few hours.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation confirmed, rollback successful, paging cleared. Monitoring window 30m.
Claire: customer notifications sent. I'll coordinate any follow-ups with account teams.
Devon: thanks all. I'll attach debug notes to the incident thread.
Maya: closing active pager — switching to retrospective.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged resolved by Lina and Maya"
